title: DropBoard
summary: A shared drop-space in the browser where people in a meeting, or one person across devices, exchange files, links and text using a short access code, with no accounts or installs.

contribution.roleNote: Fork of alx-du/dropboard by Alex Du; the repository includes a build log and executive report written as a teaching deliverable on building with AI coding tools.

narrative.problem: Moving things between people mid-meeting is still awkward: links shared in a video call chat disappear when the call ends, teammates send files across several messaging apps, AirDrop only works Apple-to-Apple, and tools like Slack, Drive or Miro assume everyone shares a workspace and accounts.
narrative.decision: Boards are ephemeral sessions joined with a short human-readable access code and no user accounts; the deployed backend is Cloudflare Workers with Durable Objects for WebSocket sync and expiry, plus R2 for files, behind a backend-agnostic frontend switch.
narrative.tradeoff: Skipping accounts keeps a board usable within seconds on any device, but the access code becomes the only barrier, so it has to be treated like a meeting link rather than a password, and nothing is kept once a session expires.
narrative.limitation: It is a working demo under a working name: AI features are deferred, the Supabase backend is only a scaffolded alternative, and open questions remain about default expiry, sustainable file-size caps, host powers and abuse reporting.
narrative.caveat: Access codes are the only barrier to a board — treat them like a meeting link, not a password. Boards are ephemeral and their content is deleted when the session expires.
